exposure: Closure of parietal peritoneum and/or rectus abdominis muscle during cesarean section
cohort: 180 patients who underwent C-section for various reasons
finding: Closing the parietal peritoneum alone after C-section was associated with higher pain scores at 6 and 12 hours post-op, but rectus abdominis muscle reapproximation did not increase pain, and neither closure type affected bowel motility.
